task: The LLM provider dialog (GenerateModal) doesn't have the required inputs: protocol (anthropic | openai), baseUrl, and modelName. The user wants CRUD for LLM providers so they can add custom providers like opencode (Go) and minimax. Today the provider set is a hardcoded static PROVIDERS array (Anthropic / OpenAI / Local), the baseUrl and free-form model inputs only appear for the local provider, ProviderId is a closed union ('anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local') threaded through providerAdapters.ts and apiKeys.ts, and the adapter's wire-format dispatch is a closed switch. A provider definition should carry: id/name, protocol ('anthropic' | 'openai'), baseUrl (origin), and a modelName. API keys stay keyed per-provider in the existing apiKeys module (separate localStorage key, never in the persisted leetlab.v2 slice, never in full-state export). Scope answers from the user: (1) DEFER full-state export/import of provider definitions this round — provider config lives only in browser localStorage; (2) built-ins are FULLY USER-MANAGED — Anthropic/OpenAI/Local are just the initial seed, any may be edited or deleted.

analysis.objective: Add full user-managed CRUD for LLM providers — a persistent provider registry (protocol, baseUrl origin, modelName) backed by its own localStorage key — and make generation dispatch on the provider's protocol instead of a hardcoded provider id, while keeping API keys in the existing apiKeys module and out of the persisted slice and export.
analysis.successDefinition: A user can, from the settings/generate UI, create, edit, and delete any provider (the Anthropic/OpenAI/Local entries are only the initial seed, fully editable and deletable); a provider definition carries id/name, protocol ('anthropic'|'openai'), baseUrl origin, and modelName; the registry survives reload in its own localStorage key (not leetlab.v2, not full-state export); generation works for a user-added custom provider by dispatching on protocol (anthropic → {baseUrl}/v1/messages with x-api-key + anthropic-version; openai → {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with Bearer key); GenerateModal derives its provider/protocol/baseUrl/modelName fields from the registry; API keys stay per-provider in leetlab.apiKeys and appear in neither the persisted slice nor the full-state export; TypeScript compiles (no remaining 3-value closed union on the generate path) and lint/build/tests pass.
assumptions: Provider ids become arbitrary strings (seeded as 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local') rather than a closed 3-value union; the wire-format dispatch keys off protocol, not provider id, and per-provider literals in the adapters ('anthropic'/'openai'/'local') for error attribution and default URLs are replaced by protocol-driven logic.
baseUrl is stored and validated as an origin (http/https); the adapter appends '/v1/messages' or '/v1/chat/completions' exactly as today.
The task's 'modelName' is a single string per provider — the built-ins' current models[] lists collapse to one default modelName that the user can edit; no per-provider model lists remain.
API keys are optional when saving a provider; auth failures surface at generation time as ProviderError category 'auth', since the old `provider !== 'local'` keyRequired rule does not generalize.
Deleting a provider also clears its stored API key from leetlab.apiKeys (avoids orphaned key material); editing a provider must preserve its id so the stored key keeps its association.

Provider registry gets its own localStorage key (e.g. leetlab.providers) separate from leetlab.apiKeys and leetlab.v2; the existing leetlab.apiKeys entries keyed 'local' remain compatible because 'local' stays a seeded id.
The GenerateModal may open with a selected provider that was just deleted; it must fall back to the first remaining provider or an empty state.
Users can delete every provider; generation then shows an empty/disabled state rather than crashing.
Browser-direct CORS constraints on custom baseUrls (opencode Go server, minimax) are the provider's responsibility and can only surface as 'cors-network' errors in-app.

This roadmap deliberately supersedes the prior roadmap's documented YAGNI gate on a dynamic provider registry; the old roadmap's closed three-provider assumptions (keyRequired = provider !== 'local', per-provider models[] catalogs) do not transfer.
risks: Widening the closed ProviderId/ApiProvider union to string ids touches apiKeys.ts, providerAdapters.ts, and GenerateModal together; if not done atomically, the generate path keeps a stale 3-value union and custom providers silently fall through the dispatch switch.
Deleting or renaming (id-changing) a provider that is currently selected in GenerateModal can leave the modal pointing at a ghost id, or orphan the stored API key if the id changes on edit.

Wrong dispatch for a custom provider (anthropic-protocol vs openai-protocol) sends the request to the wrong endpoint/path and produces confusing non-auth failures; the switch must branch on protocol with no unreachable provider-id arms.
The default-base-URL table (DEFAULT_BASE_URLS) and the `keyRequired = provider !== 'local'` rule are hardcoded to the three built-ins and will mis-handle custom providers unless generalized.
Pasting a full endpoint path instead of an origin into baseUrl produces a malformed URL when the adapter appends /v1/...; needs normalization/validation at save time.
No validation for duplicate provider names/ids could create two identical registry entries whose keys collide in the per-provider key map.

Export integration is deferred by the user, so providers do not survive a full-state restore or machine migration this round — accepted, but a user may assume providers are backed up by the existing export.

The adapter's anthropic path hardcodes the 'anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access' header and anthropic-version; a custom anthropic-protocol provider may not accept these — the header behavior should follow the protocol default, not a custom provider's assumptions.
outOfScope: Full-state export/import of provider definitions — explicitly deferred by the user; provider config lives only in browser localStorage this round (API keys stay excluded from export regardless).
Multi-model lists per provider — the task specifies a single modelName, so the built-ins' models[] catalogs are collapsed to one editable model string.
Automatic model discovery from OpenAI-compatible servers — not requested; the user types a modelName.
Changing how API keys are stored — keys remain in the existing leetlab.apiKeys module keyed per-provider; no new key storage, no keys in the persisted slice.
A backend/proxy to work around CORS for custom baseUrls — adapters remain browser-direct.
Cloud sync or cross-machine migration of providers — nothing but this browser's localStorage this round.
Modifying the persisted Zustand slice (leetlab.v2) schema — provider config deliberately stays out of it.
OAuth/token-based or otherwise non-static-key provider auth flows — only a single per-provider API key is supported.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is about machinery — a provider registry, protocol-selected wire-format adapters, and localStorage persistence for LLM API connections — not entities or rules a business domain expert would model.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The registry entity: id/name, protocol ('anthropic'|'openai'), baseUrl origin, and a single modelName.
The localStorage-backed store (own key, e.g. leetlab.providers) holding provider definitions and supporting create/edit/delete.
The wire-format selector ('anthropic' → /v1/messages, 'openai' → /v1/chat/completions) that drives adapter dispatch; replaced the closed provider-id switch.
The origin of the provider API; the adapter appends the protocol-specific path.
The single model string a provider definition uses for generation.
The generateProblemText layer that dispatches by protocol and returns raw text or a classified ProviderError.
Per-provider key material stored in leetlab.apiKeys (getKey/setKey/clearKey), never in the persisted slice or full-state export.
The initial Anthropic/OpenAI/Local provider definitions, fully user-managed (editable/deletable) and not special-cased afterwards.

discoveryFindings.finding: There is no provider registry module and no `leetlab.providers` localStorage key. The only direct localStorage consumers are zustand persist (leetlab.v2) and apiKeys.ts (leetlab.apiKeys). apiKeys.ts is the only existing pattern for an independent, lazily-read localStorage key.
discoveryFindings.implication: The registry is net-new, not a refactor of existing storage. It should mirror apiKeys.ts: its own key, defensive readAll/writeAll (corrupt JSON returns null, non-string dropped), lazy reads at call time (not module load) so the existing localStorage-shim test pattern keeps working.

discoveryFindings.finding: `ApiProvider` ('anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local') is the closed 3-value union defined in apiKeys.ts and re-exported as `ProviderId` in providerAdapters.ts; it is threaded through getKey/setKey/clearKey, ProviderError, GenerateProblemTextOptions, and GenerateModal's provider state. Critically, apiKeys' storage layer is already `Record<string, string>` — readAll/writeAll never depend on the union at runtime.
discoveryFindings.implication: Widening to arbitrary string ids is runtime-safe for the key map — no data migration; existing 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local' entries survive untouched. The widening is purely type-level but must land atomically across apiKeys.ts + providerAdapters.ts + GenerateModal.tsx or the generate path keeps a stale closed union (the task's top risk).

discoveryFindings.finding: `generateProblemText` is a closed switch over provider id with no default arm, relying on TS exhaustiveness. `generateOpenAiCompatible` takes `provider: 'openai' | 'local'` and reads `DEFAULT_BASE_URLS[provider]`; `parseAnthropicResponse`/`httpError`/`toProviderError` hardcode the 'anthropic' literal for error attribution.
discoveryFindings.implication: Widening ProviderId to string breaks the switch (non-exhaustive, needs a default), breaks `Record<ProviderId, string>` indexing in DEFAULT_BASE_URLS, and the per-provider literals for error attribution no longer hold. Dispatch must branch on protocol; error attribution literals become the passed-in provider id. These are compile errors that force the atomic refactor together with the union widening.

discoveryFindings.finding: `DEFAULT_BASE_URLS: Record<ProviderId, string>` is hardcoded to the three built-ins and consumed in exactly two places: `generateAnthropic` (`options.baseUrl ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URLS.anthropic`) and `generateOpenAiCompatible` (`options.baseUrl ?? DEFAULT_BASE_URLS[provider]`).
discoveryFindings.implication: The task's hardcoded-table concern is confirmed: the Record is typed to the closed union and its only consumers assume the three built-ins. With user-managed per-provider baseUrl coming from the registry, the adapter should take the baseUrl as required (or default to the registry value) rather than a built-in lookup.

discoveryFindings.area: Static PROVIDERS array and ProviderConfig shape
discoveryFindings.finding: `PROVIDERS` is a `readonly ProviderConfig[]` static constant. `ProviderConfig` carries `models: readonly ModelOption[]` (3 per built-in, [] for local) and optional `modelPlaceholder` — there is no single `modelName` field. GenerateModal depends on `models[0]?.id` (initial model state and on provider change).
discoveryFindings.implication: The task's assumption that models[] collapse to one editable modelName is confirmed against the actual shape. PROVIDERS becomes a seeded registry; `models[0]?.id ?? ''` fallbacks and the select-vs-free-form-input branch in GenerateModal both change, and ProviderConfig's id is no longer the closed union.

discoveryFindings.finding: GenerateModal types provider state as `ApiProvider`, seeds model from `PROVIDERS[0].models[0].id`, shows baseUrl only when `provider === 'local'`, and passes baseUrl to the adapter only when `provider === 'local'` (otherwise undefined → DEFAULT_BASE_URLS fallback). `keyRequired = provider !== 'local'` gates the submit button. There is no provider CRUD surface anywhere in the app — the modal is the only provider UI.
discoveryFindings.implication: The modal must derive provider/protocol/baseUrl/modelName from the registry. Both `keyRequired = provider !== 'local'` and the `provider === 'local'` baseUrl gate are closed-union assumptions that mis-handle custom providers. Create/edit/delete affordances are entirely net-new UI; the 'manage providers' surface does not exist and must be invented (in-modal or alongside).

discoveryFindings.finding: Export format is exactly `{version, persisted, generatedProblems}` built from an explicit allowlist (buildFullStateExport), never spreading the store; import validates the exact schema with a version gate and rejects on any mismatch. Neither module reads apiKeys. Tests assert exact top-level keys and that the exported JSON never contains 'local', 'sk-', or 'apiKeys'.
discoveryFindings.implication: Deferring provider export/import costs nothing this round: as long as the registry lives in its own localStorage key (like leetlab.apiKeys), neither fullStateExport.ts nor fullStateImport.ts needs a change and the existing exact-key tests keep passing. Any future inclusion would require a schema/version change and would break those tests.

discoveryFindings.finding: zustand persist key `leetlab.v2` with `partialize` allowlist exactly `{lang, split, lastSlug, problems, generatedProblems}`. AGENTS.md documents the per-field additive-vs-migrate policy (additive fields with safe defaults stay on leetlab.v2; transformed fields need leetlab.v3 + migrate).
discoveryFindings.implication: Provider config stays out of the slice per scope — no partialize, version, or migrate changes needed. apiKeys.ts is the established precedent for key material and config that must never reach the persisted slice or export.

discoveryFindings.finding: The completed roadmap explicitly gated a 'Provider plugin system / dynamic adapter registry' as YAGNI ('only three concrete adapters exist; a registry is speculative abstraction'), and its success definition, ubiquitous language, and test rubrics are all written around the closed three-provider model.
discoveryFindings.implication: This task deliberately reverses a prior, documented YAGNI decision. The new roadmap should call out that it supersedes that gate, and existing provider rubric assumptions (three fixed providers, provider===local key-required rule) in the old doc do not transfer.

discoveryFindings.area: Adapter hardcoded Anthropic headers and body
discoveryFindings.finding: The anthropic path hardcodes `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true`, and `max_tokens: 8192`; the openai-compatible path attaches `Authorization: Bearer` only when a key is supplied (local may omit). Response parsing for anthropic and openai is separate.
discoveryFindings.implication: Protocol-based dispatch reuses these exact wire behaviors unchanged (anthropic → /v1/messages with x-api-key + anthropic-version; openai → /v1/chat/completions with Bearer). The task's risk that a custom anthropic-protocol provider may reject the browser-access header stands — header behavior follows the protocol default, not per-provider opt-in. Endpoint path append (/v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions) is unchanged.

discoveryFindings.finding: No providerAdapters.test.ts exists; outputValidation.test.ts mocks `generateProblemText`. Tests that import modules reading localStorage at module load (store persist) install a window/localStorage shim before a dynamic import; apiKeys reads localStorage lazily on call and needs no shim. Convention: `*.test.ts` next to source, `npm run build` (tsc strict, noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters) is the typecheck gate.
discoveryFindings.implication: A new provider-registry module should read localStorage lazily (apiKeys-style) so existing shims are unaffected, and get its own `*.test.ts` following the shim pattern. Registry CRUD/dispatch tests must cover: protocol dispatch for a user-added provider, duplicate-id rejection, delete-clears-key, and the empty-registry state.

discoveryFindings.finding: 'local' is a seeded id in both PROVIDERS and ApiProvider; apiKeys stores all entries under arbitrary string keys (readAll is `Record<string, string>`), so the per-provider key map never depended on the closed union at runtime. clearKey already deletes by whatever key string is passed.
discoveryFindings.implication: Existing 'local'-keyed API keys remain compatible as long as 'local' stays a seeded registry id — matching the task assumption. Delete-clears-key (clearKey on delete) and edit-preserves-id already work mechanically; only the type params need widening to string.

requiredMaterials.name: Wire-protocol compatibility of the two named custom providers (opencode Go server, Minimax)
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The registry's protocol field is a closed 2-value union ('anthropic' | 'openai') and the adapter dispatch branches only on that field. The user's goal is to add custom providers 'like opencode (Go) and minimax', but nothing in the repo or the scope answers states which protocol each actually speaks. To confirm the design genuinely covers the stated intent — and to pick a correct protocol when a user creates such a provider, plus any realistic test fixture for a user-added provider — we must know whether each server is OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions + Bearer) or Anthropic-style (/v1/messages + x-api-key). Getting this wrong is the task's top dispatch risk (request routed to the wrong endpoint/path).
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Not in the repo (discovery confirmed only the three built-ins) and not specified in the scope answers. Acquire from official docs: opencode (sst/opencode) server/API docs and Minimax API docs (api.minimax.io), or directly ask the user to confirm which protocol each target should use before wiring tests/demo.

requiredMaterials.name: Live API credentials for end-to-end generation verification (existing Anthropic/OpenAI key, or a Minimax/opencode key)
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: The success definition requires 'generation works for a user-added custom provider'. Unit tests mock fetch / generateProblemText and therefore cannot prove the real wire path — protocol dispatch, endpoint-path append, auth headers (x-api-key + anthropic-version vs Bearer), response parsing, and the auth-failure ('auth') error path — against a live server. A single real end-to-end generation through the new protocol-driven adapter is the only way to reach full confidence in that acceptance criterion. Existing keys live only in the user's browser under leetlab.apiKeys (deliberately not in the repo or persisted slice), so the implementer cannot retrieve them.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Ask the user to supply an existing Anthropic or OpenAI API key (and, if available, a Minimax/opencode key to smoke-test a genuinely user-added custom provider) at the manual-acceptance step. Not obtainable autonomously by the implementer.

phases.name: Widen the apiKeys module to arbitrary provider-id strings
phases.goal: Change getKey/setKey/clearKey in src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts to accept any string provider id instead of the closed ApiProvider union. The storage layer is already Record<string, string>, so this is a pure type-level change with no data migration: existing 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local' entries survive untouched. Keep the ApiProvider/ProviderId alias in place for now (the generate path still uses it until the protocol-dispatch phase) so nothing downstream breaks mid-flight.
inputs: src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts (ApiProvider closed union on getKey/setKey/clearKey; readAll/writeAll already Record<string, string>)
Discovery: runtime key map never depends on the closed union; 'local'-keyed entries remain compatible as long as 'local' stays a seeded id
phases.expectedResult: apiKeys.getKey/setKey/clearKey accept any string provider id, with no change to the leetlab.apiKeys storage format or to existing key entries; existing tests still pass and tsc is clean.

rubric.label: Key material round-trips byte-for-byte under any id
rubric.ruleStatement: getKey(setKey(id, v)) must return exactly v for any string id, and clearKey must remove exactly that entry, with no normalization, trimming, encoding, or defaulting applied to either the id or the key material.
passCriteria: Storing a key under an arbitrary id (e.g. 'custom-provider') then reading it back with getKey returns the identical string, byte for byte.
clearKey(id) removes exactly that entry and leaves every other entry intact.
The widened path calls no transformation (trim, encode, normalize, default) on the id or value.
failureExamples: getKey('custom-provider') returns undefined right after setKey, or returns a different string than was stored.
The widened functions silently re-narrow with an `as ApiProvider` cast or fall back to 'anthropic' for unknown ids.

rubric.label: Existing anthropic/openai/local entries survive untouched
rubric.ruleStatement: Entries previously stored under 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local' remain addressable by those same ids, the leetlab.apiKeys storage format and keys are unchanged, and no data migration was introduced.
passCriteria: readAll/writeAll still use the same Record<string, string> format with no re-keying or renaming of ids.
An entry saved before the change under 'anthropic' (and 'openai'/'local') still resolves via getKey with that same id.
The diff contains no migration, upgrade, or versioned-key logic.
failureExamples: The change re-keys existing entries (e.g. prefixes 'provider:' onto ids), losing previously saved keys.
A migration or schema bump was added to rewrite stored entries.

rubric.label: Change is purely type-level
rubric.ruleStatement: The change alters only the type surface of getKey/setKey/clearKey; no runtime branch, validation, defaulting, error throw, or side effect was added to the storage layer.
passCriteria: git diff of src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts touches only type annotations/signatures and comments; read/write/clear logic is line-for-line identical.
No new throw, console, external call, or localStorage access was introduced in the widened functions.
Function return types and the side-effect surface are unchanged.
failureExamples: The executor added id validation, error throws, or a fallback default in the storage layer as part of 'widening'.
The diff rewrites the storage serialization or key construction even though the plan declares it a pure type change.

rubric.label: ApiProvider/ProviderId alias retained; downstream unaffected
rubric.ruleStatement: The ApiProvider (or ProviderId) alias remains declared and exported so the generate path and other consumers compile unchanged, and the phase's diff touches only src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts.
passCriteria: ApiProvider (or ProviderId) is still declared and exported for downstream use.
tsc is clean across the whole repo with no edits to any downstream consumer file.
No source file other than src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts was modified by this phase.
failureExamples: The alias was deleted, breaking imports in the generate path (compilation fails downstream).
The executor had to edit downstream files to compensate, indicating the alias was removed.

rubric.label: Widening is proven usable, not just declared
rubric.ruleStatement: A test or compile-time check exercises getKey/setKey/clearKey with an id outside the old 'anthropic'|'openai'|'local' union, proving the widened signature actually accepts arbitrary strings.
passCriteria: At least one test (or equivalent compile-time usage) calls getKey/setKey/clearKey with an id not in the old union (e.g. 'my-custom-provider').
That usage compiles and, where asserted, round-trips correctly through storage.
The existing test suite passes unchanged — no tests were deleted or edited to make the widening compile.
failureExamples: No test references a non-union id, so the widening is verified only vacuously by tsc on the function's own declaration.
A previously-passing test had to be edited or removed to accommodate the change.

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: the executor widened the signature but re-narrowed internally (an `as ApiProvider` cast or validation that rejects unknown ids) or deleted the ApiProvider alias and broke the generate path — the fastest fix is to revert apiKeys.ts to signature-only edits, restore the alias, add one test that round-trips a non-union id like 'my-custom-provider', then re-run tsc and the existing suite.

phases.name: Provider registry module backed by its own leetlab.providers localStorage key
phases.goal: Create a net-new src/infrastructure/providerRegistry.ts that defines ProviderDefinition (id, name, protocol 'anthropic' | 'openai', baseUrl origin, single modelName) and ProviderProtocol, mirrors the apiKeys.ts lazy/defensive localStorage pattern under its own 'leetlab.providers' key (corrupt JSON → null, non-string dropped, reads at call time so existing localStorage-shim tests are unaffected), seeds Anthropic/OpenAI/Local from the current DEFAULT_BASE_URLS/PROVIDERS values as the initial fully user-managed seed, and exposes getProviders/getProvider/createProvider/updateProvider/deleteProvider with validation (baseUrl must be an http/https origin and is normalized, duplicate id rejected on create, update preserves the provider id so its stored API key keeps its association, delete also calls apiKeys.clearKey to clear that provider's key). The registry deliberately never writes to leetlab.v2 or full-state export. This phase supersedes the prior roadmap's documented YAGNI gate on a dynamic provider registry (docs/done/llm-generated-problems-import-export-roadmap.md gated 'a dynamic adapter registry' as speculative abstraction); the old roadmap's closed three-provider rubric assumptions (keyRequired = provider !== 'local', per-provider models[] catalogs) do not transfer.
inputs: Existing DEFAULT_BASE_URLS and PROVIDERS constant values in src/infrastructure/providerAdapters.ts as the seed data for Anthropic/OpenAI/Local

Discovery: no provider registry or leetlab.providers key exists; apiKeys.ts is the only precedent for an independent, lazily-read localStorage key; providers stay out of the leetlab.v2 partialize allowlist and full-state export/import by construction
phases.expectedResult: A standalone provider-registry module with its own 'leetlab.providers' localStorage key providing full CRUD (duplicate-id rejection, edit-preserves-id, delete-clears-the-api-key), origin-normalizing baseUrl validation, a single editable modelName per provider, and the three built-ins as the initial seed; a new providerRegistry.test.ts covers CRUD, duplicate-id rejection, delete-clears-key, origin validation, and the empty-registry state using the lazy-read (no-shim) pattern.
phases.compensation: The registry writes only to its own 'leetlab.providers' key and never touches leetlab.v2, leetlab.apiKeys (except clearKey on delete), or full-state export/import. Rollback is a plain code revert; any rows written to 'leetlab.providers' during the phase are isolated to that key and can be discarded by clearing it, with no effect on the persisted slice or the exact-key export tests.

rubric.label: Own-key storage isolation
rubric.ruleStatement: The registry persists provider definitions only under its own 'leetlab.providers' key and never writes them to leetlab.v2, the persisted slice, or the full-state export; apiKeys is touched only via clearKey on delete.
passCriteria: Every localStorage write/read in providerRegistry.ts targets only the 'leetlab.providers' key.
The leetlab.v2 partialize allowlist / persisted slice contains no provider or providerRegistry entry.
Full-state export and import paths carry no provider-definition data.
The registry never calls apiKeys.setKey or writes key material; apiKeys is invoked only as clearKey within deleteProvider.
failureExamples: Provider definitions appear in the leetlab.v2 persisted slice or in full-state export JSON.
providerRegistry.ts writes to a localStorage key other than 'leetlab.providers'.
The registry writes or reads API key material through apiKeys.

rubric.label: Lazy defensive localStorage reads
rubric.ruleStatement: Reads of 'leetlab.providers' happen at call time (no module-level cached snapshot), and malformed payloads degrade safely: corrupt JSON yields a recoverable state rather than throwing, and non-string/foreign entries are dropped.
passCriteria: Each getProviders/getProvider call re-reads localStorage instead of returning a cached snapshot captured at module load.
A value for 'leetlab.providers' that is not valid JSON causes a defined fallback (empty or seed), not a throw.
Non-string or non-object entries inside the parsed list are dropped without throwing.
The read-at-call-time behavior keeps the existing localStorage-shim tests green.
failureExamples: getProviders caches the parsed list at import time so a later localStorage mutation is invisible.
Setting 'leetlab.providers' to '{broken json' makes getProviders throw instead of returning a fallback.
Iterating a list that contains a numeric entry crashes instead of skipping it.

rubric.label: CRUD invariants (duplicate reject, edit preserves id, delete clears key)
rubric.ruleStatement: createProvider rejects duplicate ids, updateProvider preserves the provider id so its stored API key keeps its association, deleteProvider also calls apiKeys.clearKey, and the empty-registry state is fully usable.
passCriteria: createProvider with an already-existing id is rejected and does not overwrite the existing provider.
updateProvider cannot change the provider id (rejects or ignores id edits), keeping the apiKeys association intact.
deleteProvider removes the row from 'leetlab.providers' AND calls apiKeys.clearKey(providerId).
An absent 'leetlab.providers' key yields a usable empty (or seeded) state and createProvider succeeds from that state.
failureExamples: createProvider silently overwrites an existing provider that shares the id.
updateProvider lets the caller change the id, orphaning the stored API key.
deleteProvider removes the row but leaves the key behind in leetlab.apiKeys.
getProviders returns undefined or throws when the key is absent instead of a usable list.

rubric.label: baseUrl origin validation and normalization
rubric.ruleStatement: createProvider/updateProvider validate baseUrl as an http(s) origin (scheme + host, no path beyond an optional trailing slash) and store a normalized origin the adapter can append a protocol-specific path to.
passCriteria: baseUrl values that are not http/https (ftp://, javascript:, bare hostnames) are rejected.
baseUrl values carrying a path or query (e.g., https://api.example.com/v1) are rejected or normalized down to the origin.
Trailing-slash and non-trailing-slash variants normalize to one canonical form.
The stored value round-trips as a valid origin (the adapter would not produce a doubled path like /v1/v1/messages).
failureExamples: A provider is accepted with baseUrl 'example.com' or 'ftp://host'.
The stored baseUrl retains '/v1', so the adapter appends '/v1/messages' and builds '/v1/v1/messages'.
baseUrl with and without a trailing slash are stored as two distinct, non-equal values.

rubric.label: Seeded providers are fully user-managed
rubric.ruleStatement: The initial state seeds Anthropic, OpenAI, and Local from the current DEFAULT_BASE_URLS/PROVIDERS constants, each carrying exactly one editable modelName, and the seeds are not special-cased afterwards (editable/deletable like any user provider).
passCriteria: On first load (absent key) the registry returns Anthropic, OpenAI, and Local entries whose baseUrl/protocol match the current DEFAULT_BASE_URLS/PROVIDERS values.
Each provider definition carries exactly one modelName field.
updateProvider and deleteProvider operate on the seeded providers with no built-in-exemption branch.
Seed data is derived from the shared constants rather than duplicated literal values that can drift.
failureExamples: Seeds hardcode baseUrls that already diverge from DEFAULT_BASE_URLS/PROVIDERS.
Seeded providers cannot be edited or deleted because code special-cases their ids.
A provider definition carries multiple model choices instead of a single modelName.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a storage-leak or a cached-read regression — provider definitions slipping into the leetlab.v2 partialize allowlist or full-state export, or getProviders caching its read at module load and breaking the localStorage-shim tests — so grep every localStorage access in providerRegistry.ts to confirm it targets only 'leetlab.providers' and re-reads at each call, then re-run the export/import and shim test suites.

phases.name: Protocol-driven generation pipeline (adapter dispatch + GenerateModal registry derivation)
phases.goal: Rewrite the generate path atomically (the task's top risk requires providerAdapters.ts and GenerateModal.tsx to land together): make generateProblemText dispatch on the provider's protocol — 'anthropic' → {baseUrl}/v1/messages with x-api-key + anthropic-version + browser-access header, 'openai' → {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with Bearer — with no provider-id arms and no unreachable cases; make baseUrl a required option and thread modelName through the request body; attribute errors to the passed-in provider id (string) instead of the hardcoded 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local' literals; remove DEFAULT_BASE_URLS and the static PROVIDERS array from the adapter. Rework GenerateModal to read the provider registry for its provider dropdown and derive protocol/baseUrl/modelName from the selected provider definition (single editable modelName for every provider, baseUrl input shown and pre-filled for all protocols, not just local), drop the provider==='local' baseUrl gate and the keyRequired = provider!=='local' submit rule (keys optional at save; auth failures surface at generation as ProviderError category 'auth'), pass protocol/baseUrl/modelName/providerId to the adapter, fall back to the first remaining provider when the selected provider was deleted, and render an empty/disabled state when the registry is empty. This leaves no 3-value closed provider union on the generate path.
phases.boundedContext: LLM generation pipeline (GenerateModal → provider adapter → wire format) (application)
inputs: src/infrastructure/providerAdapters.ts (closed provider-id switch with no default arm, DEFAULT_BASE_URLS Record, per-provider literals in httpError/toProviderError/parseAnthropicResponse, wire-format headers to reuse unchanged)

src/components/GenerateModal.tsx (ApiProvider state, model seeded from PROVIDERS[0].models[0].id, baseUrl gated on provider==='local', keyRequired = provider !== 'local', select-vs-free-form model branch)
apiKeys.getKey(providerId) after the widen phase (string ids)

Material: wire-protocol compatibility of the named custom providers (opencode Go server, Minimax) — confirms the 2-value protocol union covers the stated intent and supplies a realistic user-added-provider fixture

Discovery: adapters stay browser-direct with unchanged /v1/... path append and header/body wire behavior per protocol; custom anthropic-protocol providers inherit the protocol default headers, not per-provider opt-in
phases.expectedResult: The LLM generation path is registry-driven and protocol-dispatched: generateProblemText branches on protocol with a required baseUrl (origin) and modelName threaded into the request body, errors are attributed to the passed-in provider id string, and the static PROVIDERS array and DEFAULT_BASE_URLS are removed from providerAdapters.ts; GenerateModal derives its provider/protocol/baseUrl/modelName fields from the registry with a single editable modelName for every provider, no provider==='local' baseUrl gate, no keyRequired rule, a deleted-selected-provider fallback, and an empty-registry disabled state; no 3-value closed provider union remains on the generate path. New providerAdapters.test.ts proves a user-added openai-protocol provider and an anthropic-protocol provider hit the correct endpoint/path/auth header set, and that auth failures surface as ProviderError 'auth'; modal fallback/empty-state behavior is covered.

rubric.label: Adapter dispatch is protocol-only, closed-union-free
rubric.ruleStatement: generateProblemText in providerAdapters.ts dispatches solely on the provider's protocol ('anthropic' | 'openai'), with both arms handled exhaustively, no provider-id arms, no default/unreachable case, and no 3-value closed provider union driving the generate path; the static PROVIDERS array and DEFAULT_BASE_URLS are gone from the adapter.
passCriteria: No provider-id branch exists in the adapter dispatch: grep of providerAdapters.ts for 'local' or per-provider literal conditions on the generate path finds none.
Both protocol arms are explicit and exhaustive — TypeScript reports no unreachable case and no default: arm silently swallows an unknown protocol value.
'DEFAULT_BASE_URLS' and a static 'PROVIDERS' array do not appear anywhere in providerAdapters.ts.
The dispatch input is the ProviderProtocol from the registry (not a 3-value ApiProvider union), and the selected provider id flows as a plain string rather than a closed literal type.
failureExamples: A leftover `if (providerId === 'local')` or a switch on a 3-value provider union remains, so a user-added provider falls into an unreachable default arm.
DEFAULT_BASE_URLS still present, so a provider whose registry baseUrl is empty silently resolves to a hardcoded URL.
The dispatch has a default: arm that swallows an out-of-band protocol value instead of failing loudly.

rubric.label: Per-protocol wire format is correct and proven by tests
rubric.ruleStatement: The adapter builds the correct request per protocol — 'anthropic' → {baseUrl}/v1/messages with x-api-key, anthropic-version, and browser-access headers and modelName in the body; 'openai' → {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with Authorization: Bearer and modelName in the body — with baseUrl a required origin option and the /v1/... path append unchanged. The new providerAdapters.test.ts proves this for user-added providers of both protocols.
passCriteria: providerAdapters.test.ts includes a user-added openai-protocol fixture asserting a request to {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with a Bearer Authorization header and modelName in the body.

providerAdapters.test.ts includes a user-added anthropic-protocol fixture asserting a request to {baseUrl}/v1/messages with x-api-key, anthropic-version, and the browser-access header, and modelName in the body.
baseUrl is a required option (omitting it is a compile error) and is treated as an origin with the protocol-specific path appended unchanged.
modelName from the passed-in options appears in the request body for both protocol arms.
failureExamples: The openai fixture hits /v1/messages or sends x-api-key instead of Bearer, so a user-added OpenAI provider fails.
The anthropic fixture lacks the browser-access header or anthropic-version, so a custom anthropic-protocol provider is rejected by the server.
modelName is missing from one protocol's body, so generation uses a stale default model.
No user-added-provider fixture exists at all — tests only cover the seeded providers, so the protocol path is unproven.

rubric.label: Errors attributed to the passed-in provider id; auth failures surface as 'auth'
rubric.ruleStatement: Every provider error is attributed to the provider id string passed into the call (never a hardcoded 'anthropic'/'openai'/'local' literal), and authentication failures surface at generation as ProviderError category 'auth' — this is what makes keys-optional-at-save workable, since missing/wrong keys fail loudly at generation instead of being gated earlier.
passCriteria: httpError/toProviderError build the ProviderError from the passed-in providerId string; grep of the adapter error path shows no hardcoded provider-name literals.
providerAdapters.test.ts asserts that a 401 for a user-added provider resolves to ProviderError category 'auth' carrying that provider's id.
The modal has no keyRequired submit rule, so an absent/wrong key reaches generation and surfaces as the 'auth' ProviderError (verified by code inspection and, where feasible, a test).
failureExamples: A 401 from a user-added provider is classified as a generic unknown error instead of 'auth'.
The ProviderError carries a hardcoded 'anthropic' or 'local' id, breaking per-provider error attribution.
The modal still refuses to submit with no saved key, so the auth path never executes at generation.

rubric.label: GenerateModal derives all fields from the provider registry
rubric.ruleStatement: GenerateModal builds its provider dropdown and generation fields from the provider registry (not a static PROVIDERS array): it derives protocol/baseUrl/modelName from the selected provider definition, shows a baseUrl input pre-filled for every protocol (no provider==='local' gate), exposes a single editable modelName for every provider, has no keyRequired submit rule, and passes protocol/baseUrl/modelName/providerId to the adapter. All adapter call sites use the new options shape, so the adapter and modal halves landed atomically.
passCriteria: The modal imports and reads the provider registry for its dropdown; no import of a static PROVIDERS array or DEFAULT_BASE_URLS remains.
A baseUrl input is rendered and pre-filled with the selected provider's baseUrl for every protocol, and a single editable modelName field exists for every provider (no select-vs-free-form branch).
No `provider === 'local'` baseUrl gate and no keyRequired submit rule remain in the modal.
Every call site of generateProblemText passes the new options shape (providerId, protocol, baseUrl, modelName); grep finds no caller passing the old provider-id-only argument.
failureExamples: The baseUrl input is hidden or read-only for anthropic/openai providers — the old 'local'-only gate is back.
modelName is a select from PROVIDERS[0].models for some protocols and free-form for others, leaving the old branch.
The modal still blocks submit when no api key is saved (keyRequired leftover), contradicting keys-optional-at-save.
One call site still calls generateProblemText with the old argument, breaking the interface and proving the change was not atomic.

rubric.label: Modal degrades safely on registry mutation and emptiness
rubric.ruleStatement: When the selected provider has been deleted, the modal falls back to the first remaining provider and re-derives protocol/baseUrl/modelName; when the registry is empty, the modal renders an empty/disabled state in which a generate call cannot be made. Both behaviors are exercised in tests.
passCriteria: A test covers the deleted-selected-provider case: after deletion, the modal selects the first remaining provider and re-derives protocol/baseUrl/modelName (no stale providerId or model reaches the adapter).
A test covers the empty-registry case: with zero providers the modal shows an empty/disabled state and the generate action is not callable.
Both paths resolve through registry reads — no resurrection of a static PROVIDERS array to paper over the fallback.
failureExamples: Deleting the selected provider leaves a stale providerId that reaches the adapter, causing a wrong-origin or wrong-protocol call.
With an empty registry the modal still enables Generate and calls the adapter with undefined protocol/baseUrl.
The fallback re-derives only protocol/baseUrl but keeps the deleted provider's modelName.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a half-migration that leaves a 'local' provider-id arm or the keyRequired/provider==='local' gate in the modal (or DEFAULT_BASE_URLS/PROVIDERS in the adapter) while the other half is already protocol-driven — grep the generate path for 'local', 'keyRequired', 'DEFAULT_BASE_URLS', and 'PROVIDERS', delete every leftover, and add a user-added-provider fixture exercising whichever protocol arm the new tests miss.

phases.name: User-facing create/edit/delete management surface for providers
phases.goal: Add a manage-providers surface (within GenerateModal or alongside it — no provider CRUD UI exists anywhere today) that lists the provider registry and supports create, edit, and delete: a create/edit form capturing name, a protocol selector ('anthropic' | 'openai'), a baseUrl input validated as an http/https origin (rejecting pasted endpoint paths), and a single modelName; duplicate-name/id rejection surfaced in the form; edit preserves the provider id so the stored per-provider API key keeps its association; delete confirms and clears the provider's API key via the registry, and if the deleted provider was selected in GenerateModal the modal falls back to the first remaining provider or the empty state.
inputs: GenerateModal's registry-derived provider selection and deleted-selected/empty fallback from the protocol-driven-generate-path phase
Discovery: no provider CRUD surface exists anywhere in the app — this is net-new UI
phases.expectedResult: A user can, from the UI, add an arbitrary custom provider (e.g. an opencode Go server or minimax endpoint configured with the matching protocol), edit any provider including the Anthropic/OpenAI/Local seeds, and delete any provider (with its API key cleared), with the GenerateModal provider dropdown reflecting the change immediately and falling back safely when the selected provider is removed.

rubric.label: Full create/edit/delete from the manage surface, persisted
rubric.ruleStatement: The manage-providers surface lists the current registry and lets a user create, edit, and delete any provider — including the Anthropic/OpenAI/Local seeds — with every mutation persisted to the leetlab.providers localStorage key and surviving a full reload.
passCriteria: Opening the manage surface lists exactly the providers present in leetlab.providers (the three seeds on first run; seeds plus custom ones after creation), and the list is live rather than a hardcoded snapshot.

Create: filling name, a protocol selector restricted to 'anthropic'|'openai', a baseUrl, and a single modelName adds a row that appears in leetlab.providers and is still listed after a full page reload.
Edit: changing name/protocol/baseUrl/modelName on an existing provider updates its row and its leetlab.providers entry, and the change survives reload.
Delete: removing a provider removes its row and its leetlab.providers entry, and it does not reappear after reload.
The Anthropic, OpenAI, and Local seeds are editable and deletable exactly like custom providers — no provider is locked, read-only, or resurrected after deletion.
The UI cannot save a provider whose protocol is outside 'anthropic'|'openai' (the selector offers only those two values).
failureExamples: Create/edit/delete controls exist but mutations are not persisted — after reload the registry reverts to its previous state.
The list is a hardcoded or stale snapshot and does not reflect registry mutations made in the same session.
The Anthropic/OpenAI/Local seeds are editable but cannot be deleted (or reappear after reload), i.e. they are special-cased.
Deleting a provider throws or leaves a dangling entry that still appears in the list and in GenerateModal's dropdown.

rubric.label: baseUrl validated as an http/https origin
rubric.ruleStatement: The baseUrl field accepts only an http/https origin (scheme + host, no path/query/fragment) and rejects any pasted endpoint URL that includes a path, query, or fragment, with the rejection surfaced as a form error.
passCriteria: Origin-only values such as 'https://api.openai.com' and 'http://localhost:8080' save successfully.

Values containing a path are rejected with an inline form error and not saved: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/messages', 'https://api.openai.com/chat/completions', and 'https://api.openai.com/' (trailing slash).
Values with a query or fragment are rejected: 'https://host?v=1', 'https://host#beta'.
Values with a non-http(s) scheme are rejected: 'ftp://host', 'ws://host', 'file:///tmp'.
A bare host without a scheme ('api.openai.com') is rejected — a scheme is required.
The stored baseUrl in leetlab.providers is exactly the origin the user entered, with no appended or normalized path that would double up when the adapter appends the protocol path.
failureExamples: Pasting 'https://api.openai.com/v1/messages' is accepted, so generation later produces '.../v1/messages/v1/messages'.
Invalid values are silently truncated or auto-fixed instead of surfacing a form error.
A provider with 'ftp://host' or no scheme saves successfully and appears in the registry.

rubric.label: Duplicate name/id rejected and surfaced in the form
rubric.ruleStatement: Creating or editing a provider whose id or name collides with an existing provider is blocked, and the collision is surfaced as an inline form error naming the conflicting field — not a silent overwrite, an uncaught crash, or a console-only message.
passCriteria: Creating a provider with a name that already exists (e.g. a second 'Anthropic') is rejected with an inline form error and writes no registry entry.
Creating a provider whose id would collide with an existing id is rejected the same way.
Editing a provider to a name/id already held by a different provider is rejected; editing a provider to its own current name/id is allowed.
After a rejected submission the form retains the user's inputs so they can correct the conflict.
failureExamples: Submitting a duplicate name silently overwrites the existing provider in leetlab.providers.
Duplicate creation throws an uncaught error or results in two identical rows in the list.
The duplicate is saved and the error appears only in the console, not in the form.

rubric.label: Edit preserves id and key association; delete clears the API key
rubric.ruleStatement: Editing a provider preserves its id so the per-provider API key stored in leetlab.apiKeys keeps its association, and deleting a provider first requires confirmation and clears that provider's API key via the apiKeys module so no orphaned key material remains.
passCriteria: Editing a provider's name, protocol, baseUrl, or modelName leaves its id in leetlab.providers unchanged, and getKey(id) still returns the previously stored key after the edit.
Deleting a provider removes its id from leetlab.providers and getKey(id) returns no key afterward (clearKey was invoked) — no orphaned key under that id remains in leetlab.apiKeys.
Delete is gated by an explicit confirmation (e.g. a confirm dialog) before any mutation; cancelling performs no registry or key change.
failureExamples: Editing rebuilds the provider object with a fresh id, so the key stored under the old id is silently orphaned and generation loses its key.
Deleting a provider leaves its API key in leetlab.apiKeys under a now-dead id.
Delete removes the provider with no confirmation, or cancelling the confirm still deletes the provider and key.

rubric.label: GenerateModal reflects registry changes and falls back safely on delete
rubric.ruleStatement: GenerateModal's provider dropdown derives from the registry and updates immediately when providers are created, edited, or deleted; deleting the currently selected provider does not crash the modal — it falls back to the first remaining provider, or to a defined empty state when no providers remain.
passCriteria: After creating or editing a provider, it appears or updates in GenerateModal's dropdown without a reload.
Deleting the provider currently selected in GenerateModal results in the modal selecting the first remaining provider — no stale id is held and no crash occurs.
When the last provider is deleted, GenerateModal shows a defined empty state (disabled generation plus an empty-selection prompt) and never attempts generation with an undefined provider.
Closing and reopening GenerateModal shows the same registry-derived list.
failureExamples: Deleting the selected provider leaves the dropdown on a dead id, so generation is attempted with a provider that no longer exists.
GenerateModal throws an exception or renders blank after the selected provider is removed.
The dropdown is a hardcoded provider list that ignores registry changes entirely.

rubric.label: API keys never enter the provider slice or full-state export
rubric.ruleStatement: Key material stays exclusively in the leetlab.apiKeys module (getKey/setKey/clearKey) and never appears in the persisted provider registry (leetlab.providers) or in the full-state export, so a provider definition and a full-state dump can be shared without leaking secrets.
passCriteria: After setting an API key for a provider through the app, inspecting leetlab.providers shows no key field and no key value — entries contain only id/name/protocol/baseUrl/modelName.
Exporting the full app state to JSON contains no API key values anywhere in the dump.

The manage surface reads and writes keys only via the apiKeys module — no alternate persistence path for key material is introduced by this UI (no key stored inside the provider definition or form state).
After a reload, regenerating with the same provider still uses the key from leetlab.apiKeys — the key survives reload and stays associated with the provider id.
failureExamples: An 'apiKey' field appears in leetlab.providers entries after a key is set.
The full-state export JSON contains a key value, so a shared backup file leaks secrets.
The create/edit form stores the key inside the provider definition instead of leetlab.apiKeys.

phases.healerHint: If a dimension fails it is most often provider-identity-key-integrity: an edit that rebuilds the provider object with a fresh id orphans the stored key and a delete that forgets to call clearKey leaves it behind — fix by carrying the original id through update and invoking clearKey in the delete handler, then re-run the edit and delete checks.

phases.name: Build, lint, and test verification of the provider CRUD feature
phases.goal: Run the full repository build (tsc strict with noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters), linter, and test suite after the feature lands, confirming there is no remaining 3-value closed provider union on the generate path, the provider registry and apiKeys stay out of leetlab.v2 and full-state export (the existing exact-key export tests still pass unchanged), and the new providerRegistry/providerAdapters tests are green.
inputs: npm run build / lint / test gates
The success definition's compile + lint + build + test acceptance
Existing fullStateExport/fullStateImport exact-schema tests that must remain untouched
Material: live API credentials (user-supplied at manual acceptance) for one real end-to-end generation through the protocol-driven adapter, verifying a user-added custom provider works
phases.expectedResult: The repo compiles cleanly under strict TS with no stale 3-value closed union on the generate path, lint passes, and the full test suite is green including the new provider-registry and protocol-dispatch tests and the unchanged full-state export/import tests.

rubric.label: Strict TypeScript build passes without config relaxation
rubric.ruleStatement: The repository compiles under the unmodified strict tsc config (strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters) after the provider CRUD feature lands.
passCriteria: `npm run build` exits 0 on the merged feature branch.
tsconfig.json still has strict, noUnusedLocals, and noUnusedParameters enabled (no flags were relaxed to reach green).
The provider adapter, registry, and their call sites contain no type errors, no leaked `any`, and no `// @ts-ignore` suppressions.
The build result is repeatable: it also passes from a clean checkout / fresh install (CI-equivalent), not only on the author's machine.
failureExamples: `npm run build` exits non-zero with type errors in providerAdapter, providerRegistry, or the generate path.
The config was edited to disable noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters so the build would pass.
Errors are silenced with `// @ts-ignore` or a new eslint-disable/ts-nocheck rather than fixed.
Build only passes because stale node_modules/caches from the author's workspace mask a broken clean install.

rubric.label: Linter passes with no new errors attributable to the feature
rubric.ruleStatement: `npm run lint` is clean on the feature branch, and any pre-existing repo-wide lint debt is unchanged from main — the feature introduces zero new lint findings.
passCriteria: `npm run lint` exits 0 on the feature branch.
The lint delta versus main is zero: no new errors or warnings in providerAdapter, providerRegistry, the UI, or their tests.
The new source files contain no unused imports, unused variables, or unused parameters (consistent with noUnusedLocals).
failureExamples: New lint errors appear in the provider adapter/registry files or the generation call chain.
Lint is forced green by file-level `/* eslint-disable */` or disabling rules for the new files.
New files have unused imports/variables that lint flags and the author left in place.

rubric.label: Generation dispatches on protocol, not a closed provider-id union
rubric.ruleStatement: The generate path contains no remaining 3-value closed provider union and no provider-id switch: dispatch is driven solely by `provider.protocol` ('anthropic' | 'openai'), and seeded/local providers are ordinary registry rows, never special-cased.
passCriteria: A repo-wide grep for the old closed union (e.g., `'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local'`) and any provider-id->endpoint switch finds no match in or above the generate call chain.
The provider adapter reads `provider.protocol` and branches on exactly `'anthropic'` and `'openai'`, selecting /v1/messages vs /v1/chat/completions.
No `'local'` or seeded-provider special case exists anywhere in the generation path.
failureExamples: grep still finds `type ProviderId = 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local'` referenced by the generate path.
The adapter still switches on a provider id and maps ids to endpoints instead of reading `provider.protocol`.
A hardcoded `if (providerId === 'local')` branch remains in generation.

rubric.label: Provider registry and API keys excluded from full-state export
rubric.ruleStatement: The provider registry persists under its own key (leetlab.providers) and API keys stay in leetlab.apiKeys; neither the registry rows nor any key material appear in leetlab.v2 or full-state export, and the existing exact-key export/import tests pass unchanged.
passCriteria: Serializing the full app state to leetlab.v2 / full-state export contains no provider registry data (no providers array, no leetlab.providers key, no baseUrl/modelName fields).
Full-state export contains no api key material and no `apiKeys` key under any persisted slice.
The existing fullStateExport/fullStateImport exact-key tests are byte-for-byte unchanged from main and still green.
failureExamples: Full-state export JSON includes the provider registry or the apiKeys store.
The exact-key export tests were edited to tolerate extra/missing keys so they would keep passing.
API keys were moved into the persisted slice or exported state as part of the feature.

rubric.label: New provider registry and adapter tests are green and cover real behavior
rubric.ruleStatement: The providerRegistry and providerAdapters suites run in the full test run and are green, with assertions that exercise CRUD persistence and protocol dispatch rather than empty or mocked-out shells.
passCriteria: `npm test` executes the providerRegistry and providerAdapters suites and both report passing.
The registry suite covers create, edit, delete, and a persistence round-trip (state survives reload from leetlab.providers).
The adapter suite covers dispatch for both 'anthropic' and 'openai' and returns a classified ProviderError on failure.
failureExamples: The new suites are missing, skipped, or empty (`it.todo` / no assertions).
Tests only cover a single hardcoded provider; edit/delete or both protocols are untested.
Suites pass but the mocks bypass dispatch, so protocol selection is never actually asserted.

rubric.label: A user-added custom provider generates through the protocol-driven adapter
rubric.ruleStatement: With a live API key at manual acceptance, a user can add a custom provider (protocol + baseUrl + modelName), select it, and receive real generated text through the protocol-driven adapter — not a fallback to a hardcoded provider.
passCriteria: Adding a custom provider via the registry UI and selecting it yields real generated text using the supplied live key.
The outgoing request targets the protocol-specific path (e.g., /v1/chat/completions for an openai-protocol provider) appended to the configured baseUrl origin.
The custom provider's modelName is the model used for generation.
failureExamples: Generation fails, or silently falls back to a hardcoded/seed provider, when a custom provider is selected.
The adapter ignores protocol and baseUrl and always calls the same endpoint for every provider.
The configured modelName is ignored and a default model is sent instead.

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: the gates go green only because an exact-key export/import test was loosened or a stale 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local' provider-id union still sits on the generate path — grep the generate path for the old closed union and diff the export-test files against main, fix the real code, then re-run build + lint + test from a clean checkout.

successCriteria: A user can, from the settings/generate UI, create, edit, and delete any provider (the Anthropic/OpenAI/Local entries are only the initial seed, fully editable and deletable); a provider definition carries id/name, protocol ('anthropic'|'openai'), baseUrl origin, and modelName; the registry survives reload in its own localStorage key (not leetlab.v2, not full-state export); generation works for a user-added custom provider by dispatching on protocol (anthropic → {baseUrl}/v1/messages with x-api-key + anthropic-version; openai → {baseUrl}/v1/chat/completions with Bearer key); GenerateModal derives its provider/protocol/baseUrl/modelName fields from the registry; API keys stay per-provider in leetlab.apiKeys and appear in neither the persisted slice nor the full-state export; TypeScript compiles (no remaining 3-value closed union on the generate path) and lint/build/tests pass.

widen-api-key-provider-ids: apiKeys.getKey/setKey/clearKey accept any string provider id, with no change to the leetlab.apiKeys storage format or to existing key entries; existing tests still pass and tsc is clean.

provider-registry-module: A standalone provider-registry module with its own 'leetlab.providers' localStorage key providing full CRUD (duplicate-id rejection, edit-preserves-id, delete-clears-the-api-key), origin-normalizing baseUrl validation, a single editable modelName per provider, and the three built-ins as the initial seed; a new providerRegistry.test.ts covers CRUD, duplicate-id rejection, delete-clears-key, origin validation, and the empty-registry state using the lazy-read (no-shim) pattern.

protocol-driven-generate-path: The LLM generation path is registry-driven and protocol-dispatched: generateProblemText branches on protocol with a required baseUrl (origin) and modelName threaded into the request body, errors are attributed to the passed-in provider id string, and the static PROVIDERS array and DEFAULT_BASE_URLS are removed from providerAdapters.ts; GenerateModal derives its provider/protocol/baseUrl/modelName fields from the registry with a single editable modelName for every provider, no provider==='local' baseUrl gate, no keyRequired rule, a deleted-selected-provider fallback, and an empty-registry disabled state; no 3-value closed provider union remains on the generate path. New providerAdapters.test.ts proves a user-added openai-protocol provider and an anthropic-protocol provider hit the correct endpoint/path/auth header set, and that auth failures surface as ProviderError 'auth'; modal fallback/empty-state behavior is covered.

provider-crud-ui: A user can, from the UI, add an arbitrary custom provider (e.g. an opencode Go server or minimax endpoint configured with the matching protocol), edit any provider including the Anthropic/OpenAI/Local seeds, and delete any provider (with its API key cleared), with the GenerateModal provider dropdown reflecting the change immediately and falling back safely when the selected provider is removed.

build-lint-verify: The repo compiles cleanly under strict TS with no stale 3-value closed union on the generate path, lint passes, and the full test suite is green including the new provider-registry and protocol-dispatch tests and the unchanged full-state export/import tests.
deferred: Full-state export/import of provider definitions — explicitly deferred by the user; provider config lives only in browser localStorage this round (API keys stay excluded from export regardless).
Multi-model lists per provider — the task specifies a single modelName, so the built-ins' models[] catalogs are collapsed to one editable model string.
Automatic model discovery from OpenAI-compatible servers — not requested; the user types a modelName.
Changing how API keys are stored — keys remain in the existing leetlab.apiKeys module keyed per-provider; no new key storage, no keys in the persisted slice.
A backend/proxy to work around CORS for custom baseUrls — adapters remain browser-direct.
Cloud sync or cross-machine migration of providers — nothing but this browser's localStorage this round.
Modifying the persisted Zustand slice (leetlab.v2) schema — provider config deliberately stays out of it.
OAuth/token-based or otherwise non-static-key provider auth flows — only a single per-provider API key is supported.

Provider definitions in full-state export/import — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): explicitly deferred by the user this round; discovery confirms the registry's own leetlab.providers key leaves fullStateExport/fullStateImport and their exact-key tests untouched, so deferring costs nothing.

Per-provider model lists/catalog — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): the task specifies a single modelName, so the built-ins' models[] catalogs collapse to one editable string; no per-provider model lists remain.
Automatic model discovery from OpenAI-compatible servers — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): not requested; the user types a modelName.
OAuth/token-based or otherwise non-static-key provider auth flows — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): out of scope; only a single per-provider API key is supported.
Backend/proxy to work around browser CORS for custom baseUrls — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): out of scope; adapters stay browser-direct and CORS failures surface as ProviderError 'cors-network'.

Interface/port around the provider registry (e.g. an IProviderRegistry abstraction) — fails YAGNI gate 3 (speculative abstraction): no second implementation is on the horizon, and the apiKeys precedent is a plain module with no port, so wrapping the registry in one is ceremony.

Reset-to-defaults / restore-seeded-providers feature — fails YAGNI gate 2 (not needed now): not asked for; the seeds are fully user-managed (editable/deletable) and a restore button is speculative convenience.

Per-provider override of the anthropic wire headers (e.g. omitting anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access for a custom anthropic-protocol provider) — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): scope says header behavior follows the protocol default, not per-provider opt-in.
